chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father (peace be upon him) said: 'No man strikes one part of the Quran with another except that he disbelieves.'

key_terms.بَعْضَهُ بِبَعْضٍ: one part with another (referring to cross-referencing or contrasting different verses)
key_terms.ضَرَبَ: to strike, to hit, or to compare/contrast (in the context of interpreting verses against each other)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'strike' the Quran with itself and why does it lead to disbelief?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, highlights the principle of *ta'wil* (interpretation) where selective or contradictory exegesis leads to *kufr*. In Shia scholarship, this is often understood as distorting the Quran’s meaning to suit personal desires or sect-specific biases, thereby negating its coherent message. It serves as a warning against using specific verses to nullify others without proper contextual or authoritative guidance.
